name: Andorra

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. Population on 1 January 2019: 76177 inhabitants. Eurostat dataset demo_pjan, read through the dissemination API. Andorra carries no row more recent than 2019 in that dataset, so this is the latest published figure it offers, not a current one. The year field carries that and must be read with the value: the figure is sourced, it is simply 7 years old. The previous value was an opening estimate made with no source and no research. A national statistical office would give something fresher and has not been opened here.

Searched on 2026-07-27, in Catalan, as part of the transversal venues pass over the smallest countries. Zero, and it is the most recent of the three because Andorra is in the act of acquiring puppetry rather than lacking it. The Escena Nacional d'Andorra is launching a puppet theatre project for the 2026 season, with the Valencian company Abast Teatre, a small cast to be recruited locally and a first showing at the Ànima festival. What makes this a zero rather than a one is what the article says about the starting point: its director calls puppetry a world largely unknown in the country until now, and the piece names no Andorran puppetry venue and no Andorran puppetry company, the craft being brought in from Valencia. A project with a foreign partner and no permanent ensemble is what the denominator excludes by name. The country's theatre rooms — the Teatre Comunal in Andorra la Vella, the Teatre de les Fontetes in La Massana, the Valireta hall in Encamp — are municipal general-purpose venues, and none is a puppetry unit. The previous value was the same zero, produced with no research.

Web check of 2026-07-27. No establishment retained. Andorra has a single higher education institution, the University of Andorra, whose provision covers nursing, computing, business administration and education, with no drama faculty or higher arts school. In the absence of any higher arts education in the country, no specialised higher training in puppetry arts can exist. Upper bound held at 0 for that reason, rather than raised to 1 as in countries that do have theatre education where a candidate could have escaped the search. Estimate: the argument rests on the size of the higher education system, not on a source read.

DISPUTED. First value produced as a mean conditioned on artists who actually tour, which drops from the denominator the makers who do not perform. Method error identified: a fee is not a performance. For France the true median probably sits between 10 and 20, over a bimodal distribution. For countries with permanent companies, recomputed from the top: 250 to 400 performances a year, casts of 3 to 5, a company of about twenty, so on the order of 50 to 90.
